name: Salt flat
notes: Bare salt crust in the centre with a thin ring of succulent halophytes (glasswort, iodine bush, seepweed) and saltgrass at the margins, greasewood and tamarisk on the outer rim; Bonneville/Death Valley playas, Saharan chotts, Central Asian sabkhas, Salar de Uyuni.

shrub.silhouette: spiny grey-white shrub with bright green thread leaves

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling with 2 long, narrow, fleshy cotyledons and a coiled embryo that uncoils fast; first leaves bright green, fleshy and cylindrical (1-4 cm) like the adult's. Grows slowly into a stiff, rigid, much-branched spiny shrub with pale bark; after 12 years only about 0.7 m tall on dry sites. Resprouts from the root crown.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Sarcobatus vermiculatus (transplants 0.73 m tall after 12 yr; to 3 m; vigorous crown sprouting); USDA Woody Plant Seed Manual Sarcobatus (67-91% germination in 2-10 days at 10 C); lifespan estimated from its slow growth

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS and Woody Plant Seed Manual Sarcobatus (monoecious, wind-pollinated; male flowers in small cone-like spikes at twig tips, female flowers single in leaf axils; tan winged utricles 4-5 mm, 1 cm across the wing, mature late Sep-Nov, a few hang until next summer)

leaf.note: leaves reduced to minute fleshy scales on succulent jointed branchlets

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: two small fleshy cotyledons, then succulent, jointed, bead-like green stems with only tiny scale leaves, like a miniature pickleweed. It branches from the base into a low, knobbly bush of upright jointed green stems whose segments are often nearly round; the lower stems turn woody and grey, and the plant traps blown sand and salt crust into a hummock.
growth.source: Wikipedia (low shrub to 1.8 m of alkali flats; knobby fleshy jointed green stems with scale leaves; seeds eaten in prehistory) and Gul & Weber 1999 (Can. J. Bot.: fast germination in fresh to saline water). Growth rate, first seed and lifespan estimated from related perennial chenopod shrubs.

fruiting.source: Estimated from floras (Jepson / Intermountain Flora as recalled: tiny flowers 3-5 per fleshy bract in cylindric spikes 5-25 mm at the stem tips, summer, wind-pollinated; utricle ~1 mm; spikes break up in autumn) and Wikipedia (seeds ground for food in prehistory).

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling with two fleshy cotyledons, then small, fleshy, bluish-grey wedge-shaped leaves notched at the tip, like the adult's; young twigs are downy. It branches into a stiff, tangled, spine-tipped little shrub that traps blowing sand, so older plants sit on rounded sand hummocks (nabkhas) on saline flats and coastal dunes.
growth.source: Wikipedia Nitraria retusa (to 2.5 m, rarely over 1 m; fleshy bluish-grey leaves 10-15 mm; small sweet-scented whitish-green flowers; red edible drupe 5-10 mm; salt marshes, saline semi-deserts, builds nabkhas); growth, ages and germination estimated

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (small, sweetly scented whitish or greenish 5-part flowers in small cymes; triangular drupe 5-10 mm turning red, edible and enjoyed by people and eaten by birds, camels and goats); spring flowering in the Sahara-Arabian range; set, ripening and crop estimated

leaf.note: plume foliage: scale leaves on fine, wiry, much-branched twigs read as soft feathery sprays, never as a solid mass

flower.form: dense pink plumes 2-5 cm on the twig tips

shrub.silhouette: feathery see-through plume bush with weeping whip twigs

growth.juvenile_note: Germinates within hours on wet sand or silt left by a flood; the seedling is a minute two-leaved sprout that grows 2-5 mm a day, with a ~12 cm shoot over a longer root by 8 weeks. It becomes a dense, multi-stemmed shrub of reddish-brown stems and feathery grey-green scale-leaved twigs, pink-plumed in summer, and resprouts hard after fire or cutting.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Tamarix spp. (germination <24 h; seed viable ~24-45 days in summer; seedlings 2-5 mm/day in month 1, 11.7 cm shoot at 8 weeks; may flower in year 1, most from year 3; 4-8 m, usually <6 m; resprouts 3-4 m in one season; shrubs 75-100 yr old show no decline). Height-age curve estimated from these.

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS Tamarix spp. (5 sepals and petals, dense racemes of ~20 flowers per 2.5 cm on new growth; insect cross-pollinated, wind unlikely; ~22 ovules, 8-20+ tiny plumed seeds per flower; up to 2.5 x 10^8 seeds per plant per year, shed all season). Flower life, ripening and capsule persistence estimated.

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal seedling with two fleshy, strap-like cotyledons, then small, fleshy, half-round blue-green leaves crowded along a thin stem. It hardens into a woody-based, densely branched evergreen bush of glaucous succulent leaves, often forming low hummocks on shingle at the top of salt marshes; leaves may redden in winter.
growth.source: Wikipedia Suaeda vera (small shrub of arid salt flats and salt marshes; in Britain mainly where shingle meets salt marsh; seeds germinate more readily in fresh than in salt water). Stature (to ~1.2 m), growth rate, age at first flowering and lifespan estimated from shrubby halophytes.

fruiting.source: British flora accounts (tiny green petal-less flowers 1-3 in the leaf axils, Jul-Oct; fruit a utricle in the persistent fleshy perianth with one shiny black seed ~1-1.5 mm). Pollination, ripening, persistence and crop estimated from Suaeda biology.

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling with 2 fleshy, finger-like green cotyledons, then a leafless, jointed, succulent green stem (the tiny leaves are fused into the segments) that branches into a little candelabra 10-30 cm tall. Flowers hide in the joints late in summer; the whole plant turns red or purple in autumn, sheds seed and dies.
growth.source: Davy, Bishop & Costa 2001, Biological Flora of the British Isles: Salicornia (spring germination on the marsh after rain lowers salinity, flowering Aug-Sep, seed shed in autumn, strictly annual); Wikipedia S. europaea (shoots harvested Jun-Aug, turns red/purple in autumn, edible)

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings are rare (germination is episodic, needing fresh water on saline ground); the seedling is a small tuft of short, stiff, grey-green leaves in two neat opposite ranks. Scaly rhizomes then run through the soil and send up rows of short, stiff, leafy shoots, forming a dense, low turf patch; male and female plants are separate.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Distichlis spicata (dioecious; seeds need stratification and scarification, germination rare and episodic, seedling survival 0-95% with falling salinity; rhizomes to 180 cm long, 10-25 cm deep; 15-45 cm tall, usually <30 cm; photosynthesis rises with light). Time to flowering and clone lifespan estimated.
